To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the H+-ATpase pump in osteoclasts is polarized at the ruffled membrane in response to a calcium-deficient state.
the vacuolar H+ pump is polarized at the osteoclast membrane that is attached to bone, and that this polarization is enhanced by a calcium-deficient dietary regimen.

a calcium-deficient dietary regimen resulted in an increased number of osteoclastic H+-ATPases polarized at the ruffled membrane, but did not result in a significant change in total number of osteoblasts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of osteoclast function by calcium and the mechanism(s) involved.
the regulation of the proton pump and the Cl−-H+-exchanger in avian osteoblasts and osteoclasts in vivo.
the regulation of the osteoclastic H+-ATP pump by dietary calcium and the role of the anion exchanger, erythrocyte protein, band-3, in osteoclast acid secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H+-AT Pase is polarized in osteoclasts in a calcium-deficient state.

the H+-ATpase is polarized at the osteoclast ruffled membrane and that calcium deficiency increases this degree of polarization, whereas the Cl−-H+ anion exchanger is localized at the osteoclastic basolateral membrane.
the H+-AT Pase is polarized to the ruffled membrane of osteoclast in response to a calcium-deficient dietary condition, but the band-3 anion exchanger is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

although the band-3 anion exchanger is always polarized at the basolateral surface, the vacuolar type ATPase pump can be evenly distributed or polarized at the ruffled membrane depending on dietary calcium status.
the H+-AT Pase pump in osteoclasts is more polarized to the bone surface with a calcium-deficient dietary regimen and that the anion exchanger is always polarized to the basolateralmembrane.

the H+-ATPOase pump is polarized in a significant number of osteoclastic cells in response to calcium-deficient diet and that the band-3 Cl−-H+ anion exchanger is always located at the basolateral plasma membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H+-ATPsase and Cl−/HCO3− exchange protein are polarized differently, and that the degree of H+ pump polarization is modulated by dietary calcium.
the band-3 anion exchanger is polarized at the basolateral domain of osteoclast plasma membrane, and this polar expression is not affected by the calcium-deficient diet.

osteoclast polarization for the H+- ATPase pump is not a prerequisite for bone resorption and that the Cl−-H+ anion exchanger, which is localized to the plasma membranes that do not contact the bone surface, may not play a role in the acidification of the subosteoclastic microenvironment.
